## First, choose your diving format

Ocean, Caribbean, and freshwater locations differ in conditions, depth, season, and required experience. We first establish your training level and preferred type of dive, then choose a location.

## Diving can be part of a longer journey

If diving occupies several days, the rest of the trip can focus on cities, nature, or beaches. When planning the itinerary, we account for flights and the necessary interval after diving; details are confirmed with a specialist operator.

## The event is at the heart of the journey

In this selection, the celebration is a central part of the trip, not merely mentioned in a city description. Other destinations, nature excursions, and a beach holiday can be added before and after the event.

Dates, tickets, accommodation category, and included activities are checked for the specific offer when booking. Archived programs are excluded from the selection.

## Wine and food can shape the itinerary

In Mendoza, it is easy to devote several days to wineries. In large cities, the gastronomic portion can be combined with markets, walks, museums, and conventional sightseeing.

## From wineries to cooking classes

An itinerary can include wineries, farms, markets, restaurants, and cooking classes. On a multi-country journey, it is better to alternate these stops so that each reveals local cuisine in its own way.

## The road determines the itinerary

Patagonia, the Andes, the Atacama, Brazil's coast, and the roads of Central America offer entirely different riding experiences. Before setting off, decide whether you prefer paved roads, mixed surfaces, or an itinerary with a substantial off-road component.

## Don't turn the journey into a race

Distances on a map can be misleading: elevation, road quality, weather, and border crossings all affect travel times. Plan daily mileage so that you still have energy for stops, walks, and rest.

## Nature you'll want to see with your own eyes

The power of Iguazú Falls, the blue ice of Patagonia, Andean mountain peaks, sand dunes, and Amazonian forests. Each destination brings its own scenery, walks, and opportunities to feel closer to nature.

## What nature journeys include

Itineraries may feature viewpoints, walks through national parks, and trips to volcanoes, canyons, and lakes. Read the chosen tour's program carefully: some journeys proceed at a relaxed pace, while others involve long treks. Wildlife enthusiasts can also choose the separate [“Wildlife and Safari” interest](/interests/wildlife/).
